lines: css/ holds committed files that this build does not write:
css/: 63 files in the checkout, and not one file out of the rebuild.

A directory the build writes nothing into is source under the name of an output directory, which is where a Nextcloud app keeps the scripts and stylesheets it loads from PHP with addScript and addStyle. It is left out of the comparison.
11 committed files in css/ are source, not build output, and left out of the comparison:
css/style.css: named in lib/Controller/MapController.php, and left as it is by the build

The build reads what the source imports, so those files stay in the rebuilt tree. A file the app names in PHP, a template or info.xml, or in a script by its full path, is loaded by that name, and so is what it imports. Where no build writes other bytes under such a name, the file is a hand-written script, stylesheet or asset.
npm ci and npm run build succeed on the tracked files alone, twice, in 93.5 s.
Nothing else was in the tree, which is the state a fresh clone and CI build in, so a build that needs a leftover from an earlier one would have failed here.
Every file in js/ is what this source builds.
